implementation_notes: Rust's creation owner is the smart constructor: private fields plus Order::new(raw) -> Result<Order, DomainError>, or the standard trait form TryFrom<RawOrder> so that try_into() and the ? operator perform the validation, after which the type system guarantees that any Order in scope is valid. Serde closes the deserialization hole: #[serde(try_from = "RawOrder")] routes derived Deserialize through the TryFrom implementation, so persisted or inbound data cannot bypass validation, while From/Default remain the infallible cases. This is the library-backed realization - the traits and derive machinery exist, but the domain decision stays in the TryFrom implementation.
pitfalls: derive(Deserialize) without #[serde(try_from)] builds the struct field by field and bypasses the smart constructor entirely - the classic invariant hole.
TryFrom::Error must implement Display for serde's derived path; a bare custom enum without it produces an opaque conversion error.
Making fields pub(crate) or pub re-opens direct construction; keep them private to the module when the invariant is load-bearing.
